Experimental. An organizational unit in Active Directory, run on a domain controller. Settings left unset are left as they are.

**Experimental.** Windows support is new, and this module may change between releases.

Use `windows_ad_ou` to keep an organizational unit in Active Directory. Run it on a domain controller: that's where your SSH login is a domain account.

## Example usage

```hcl
step "lab_ou" {
  windows_ad_ou {
    name        = "Lab"
    description = "Made by Conn3x"
  }
}
```

An OU inside another one names its parent in `path`:

```hcl
step "servers_ou" {
  windows_ad_ou {
    name = "Servers"
    path = "OU=Lab,DC=lab,DC=example,DC=com"
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string | No | Description. |
| `name` | string | Yes | OU name, such as Servers. |
| `on_remove` | string | No | What happens in the domain when this resource is removed: "forget" (default) leaves the OU; it never deletes one that's protected or not empty, "delete" deletes it. |
| `path` | string | No | Distinguished name of the parent, such as OU=Lab,DC=lab,DC=example,DC=com. Unset is the top of the domain. Changing it makes a new OU. |
| `protected` | bool | No | Whether the OU is protected from accidental deletion. Unset, a new OU is protected, as Windows does. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_windows_ad_ou.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the OU matched at the last refresh. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_windows_ad_ou` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.

## How it works

**Where it runs.** On a domain controller, after the reboot that finishes its promotion, so follow [`windows_ad_forest`](windows_ad_forest.md) with a reboot. On a member server with the AD tools installed it would still fail, because a key login there has no domain credentials to reach AD with.

**Waiting for AD.** Straight after a DC reboots, Active Directory can answer for the domain a minute before its global catalog does, and a write made in that minute can hang. So apply first waits until a query through the global catalog works too, for up to 10 minutes, then fails with the reason AD last gave. A write that gets no answer at all runs once more when AD answers again. It reads first, so it only writes what's still missing. A host that isn't a DC isn't waited on.

**Finding it.** The OU is looked up by `name` directly under `path`, or under the top of the domain when `path` is unset. So changing either plans a new OU, and the old one is forgotten, not moved.

**Protection.** Windows protects a new OU from accidental deletion, and so does Conn3x unless you set `protected = false`. Leave `protected` unset to keep whatever the OU has.

**Drift.** A refresh reads the description and the protection flag. If someone changes either in Active Directory Users and Computers, the next plan shows the step out of sync, and `conn3x drift` exits 2.

**Reads change nothing.** A refresh only runs `Get-ADObject` and `Get-ADOrganizationalUnit`. A host without the ActiveDirectory module reads as having no OU, rather than failing.

## Removal

By default, deleting a `windows_ad_ou` step leaves the OU and everything in it. With `on_remove = "delete"` Conn3x deletes it, but only when it's empty and not protected: it never deletes what's inside an OU. Set `protected = false` and apply first, then remove the step.
